title: QR Code Generator
dek: Links, Wi-Fi passwords, plain text — as PNG or SVG, in any colour, at any size worth needing.
meta: Create QR codes for links, text or Wi-Fi in custom colours and sizes — download as PNG or SVG. Free, browser-based, forever.

steps.p: A URL, a phone number, Wi-Fi credentials in their standard format, an SMS template, a chunk of text.
Foreground and background colours, output size, and the quiet-zone margin that scanners quietly need.
SVG for printing at any size without a single pixel of blur.

faq.a: Dark-on-light with real contrast scans reliably; light-on-dark and low-contrast pairs fail on many phone cameras. The tool warns if you drift into risky territory.
Comfortably: a few hundred characters. At that point the code gets dense and needs to be printed bigger to scan from a distance.

title: QR Code Reader
h1: Read a QR code from an image
dek: Point it at a screenshot or photo of a QR code and get the content out — no phone needed.
meta: Decode QR codes from screenshots or photos — links, text, Wi-Fi details — without a phone camera. Free, private, in-browser.

steps.b: Drop an image with a QR code
steps.p: A clean screenshot is easiest; photos work if the code fills a fair part of the frame.
Links are clickable, text is copyable, Wi-Fi strings are broken into readable parts.
The preview lets you read a URL before you visit it — the entire reason to decode one somewhere safe.

faq.a: This page reads images, not cameras — most phones already do the camera dance natively. Screenshot the code and drop it here.

faq.q: It didn't find a code — why?
faq.a: Glare, blur, or a code too small in frame. Crop tighter so the code fills the image and try again.

title: Barcode Generator
dek: CODE128, EAN and friends as crisp PNGs — for product labels, inventory stickers and shelf tags.
meta: Generate barcodes (CODE128, EAN-13, UPC, CODE39, ITF) as high-resolution PNGs in your browser. Free, private, no sign-up.

steps.p: Numbers for retail formats, anything-as-is for CODE128. The tool validates as you type.
CODE128 for general use; EAN-13 and UPC-A for retail products, where the check digit is handled for you.
Rendered at print resolution — 2–3 pixels per module scans well from a phone.

faq.a: EAN-13 for most of the world, UPC-A for North America. Both need exactly the right digit count — the tool tells you when you're off.
Yes, at print quality. Print at 300 DPI or higher, keep bars black on white, and don't stretch the proportions.

title: Create ZIP
dek: Gather loose files — or a whole folder — into one tidy ZIP, with per-file compression you can set.
meta: Create ZIP archives from files or entire folders in your browser, with compression levels and no uploads. Perfect for batches and email.

steps.b: Drop files, or choose a folder
steps.p: Folder mode keeps the whole structure inside the ZIP — subdirectories and all.
Maximum for documents, fast for photos and anything already compressed.
Named how you like, sized how you see — the final size is shown before download.

faq.a: Text, code and documents shrink a lot. JPGs, MP4s and other already-compressed files barely move — the ZIP is still worth it for bundling, not size.
Memory-bound: a couple of GB of files is realistic on a modern machine.

title: Extract ZIP
dek: Open a ZIP and take what you need — the whole thing, or only the files you actually wanted.
meta: Open ZIP archives in your browser, preview and pick individual files, or extract everything. No uploads — your archive stays local.

steps.p: The contents list appears with folder structure and sizes.
Pull out one file, or a selection — no need to unpack a 200-file archive to reach one PDF.
Individual files directly, or everything as a fresh ZIP if you want the structure kept.

faq.a: ZIP is what this reads — the rest of the world's RAR/7z files will need a desktop tool; they're mostly compressed data with more exotic algorithms.
Not supported — and honestly, encryption worth having is worth the desktop tool that handles it properly.

title: Gzip / Gunzip
dek: The humble .gz — pack a file or text into gzip format, or open one back up for reading.
meta: Compress files and text to GZIP format or decompress .gz files right in your browser. Fast, private, nothing uploaded anywhere.

steps.b: Drop a .gz file or paste text
steps.p: Log files, exports, API responses saved via curl — all common in the wild.
Decompress .gz to see its contents, or compress text/files into a .gz.
The decompressed content lands as a file, ready for a text editor.

faq.a: No — gzip compresses one stream, no file names, no archive. .zip bundles several files. The tools here each do what their format does.

faq.q: A .tgz file — can this open it?
faq.a: Not here; .tgz is gzip wrapped around a tar archive, and needs archive handling first. If it matters, say so via the contact page.

title: OCR
h1: Read text from images and scans
dek: Screenshots, photos of paper, scanned PDFs — pulled into selectable, searchable text by OCR that runs on your device.
meta: Extract text from images and scanned PDFs with on-device OCR. English supported, private — scans never leave your browser.

steps.b: Drop an image or scanned PDF
steps.p: PNG, JPG or a PDF — scanned pages are rendered and read page by page.
First use downloads the recognition engine (~11 MB, once). Then it works through the pages, with progress shown.
Copy it, download as .txt, and fix the inevitable couple of misreads — 'rn' versus 'm' remains a human specialty.

faq.a: English for now. More languages mean more megabytes, so they're added one at a time rather than all at once.
Clean digital renders and sharp scans: excellent, better than 99% on normal text. Phone photos of curved paper: entirely readable, with a few corrections needed.
No. Recognition runs in the tab, on your machine — which is also why it takes real seconds instead of a server's instant score. The trade is understood and accepted here.

title: Unit Converter
dek: Length, mass, temperature, volume, area, speed, data — with the answer appearing as you type.
meta: Convert length, weight, temperature, volume, area, speed and data units instantly. Clean browser tool, free, no ads or uploads.

steps.p: Seven shelves of units, from millimetres to nautical miles.
Both directions convert live; the factor used is shown for doubters and students.
Full precision shown, sensible rounding applied.

faq.a: Temperature has an offset, not just a multiplier — 0° doesn't mean 'no temperature'. It's handled correctly, unlike the multiplying-by-1.8 school of conversion.
Both shown where it matters: decimal (1000, what drive makers print) and binary (1024, what the file system means). The eternal discrepancy, finally on speaking terms.

title: Number Base Converter
dek: Binary, octal, decimal, hex — any of them to any of them, with the working shown.
meta: Convert between binary, octal, decimal and hexadecimal — or any base up to 36. Steps shown as well as results. Free, private.

steps.p: In whichever base you have it — set the input base first.
Binary, octal, decimal and hex at once, plus a custom base box for base 3, base 32 and the rest.

steps.b: Copy in the format you need
steps.p: Plain, or with 0x/0b prefixes for pasting into code.

faq.q: Why binary for 255 is long — got a shortcut?
faq.a: That's what 255 is in binary, and the box shows the nibble grouping (1111 1111) to make it readable. Hex exists precisely because nobody enjoys reading raw binary.
The sign is kept on the output; two's-complement representation is a deeper rabbit hole left to your language of choice.

title: Color Converter
dek: HEX, RGB, HSL — pasted from anywhere, in every format you might need next, with a live swatch.
meta: Convert colours between HEX, RGB, HSL and more with live preview. Includes contrast checks and shade steps. Free and private.

steps.p: Any format — #3B82F6, rgb(59,130,246), hsl(217,91%,60%) — detected automatically.
Every format shown in copyable rows, plus a live swatch so your eyes confirm what the numbers say.

steps.b: Check it against white and black
steps.p: Contrast ratios are shown for both, with the WCAG threshold marked — the quiet accessibility service this tool insists on.

faq.q: Why do the HSL numbers look different from my design app?
faq.a: HSL is a transform, not storage. A designer's picker can be HSL-based while the file stores HEX; the actual colour is identical.

faq.q: What contrast ratio do I need?
faq.a: 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text — AA. The card says whether you're above or below, so you find out here rather than from an accessibility audit.
